LEARNING PATH LESSON · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

Star — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson hands over the deck’s most magical shape: points to count, a twinkle to perform, and wobbly star drawings that count exactly as much as neat ones.

What is this?

A star is the shape with points all the way round — five on this card — straight from the night sky, and the word printed for toddlers underneath.

What does it mean?

Counting points on a star is counting with a purpose and a natural stop: the points run out. Purposeful counting like this is where numbers start meaning something.

What does the child need to know?

The twinkle is the action version — fingers opening and closing in the air, sparkle included. Action-and-shape pairs stick twice as hard as shapes alone.

Why this matters

Stars carry the night sky, the Christmas tree and every reward chart ever printed. The shape comes pre-loaded with excitement, which pays the lesson’s bills.

What it teaches

Counting points on a fixed target, finger-and-arm twinkle coordination, and shape-drawing courage — wobbly is welcome, and wobbly is how drawing starts.

Words to learn

starpointtwinkleskyshinefive

Say this to your child

“"A star! Look at all its points. Can you count them with me? One… two… three… four… five! Now twinkle — fingers open, fingers shut. Twinkle, twinkle, little star!"”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and say star, then count the points with one slow finger — one, two, three, four, five.
  2. Twinkle together: hands up high, fingers opening and shutting, a little twinkle sound included. Sparkle is mandatory.
  3. Hunt stars in books, on clothes, on the reward chart — counting the points at each find, even the four-pointed rebels.
  4. When your toddler’s count reaches three or six, take the count and keep the finger slow; precision arrives with practice, delight arrives now.
  5. Close the week with a star-drawing session — wobbly lines welcome — and tape the results to the window for the sky to see.

Look closer at the picture

This card is the star card — one pointed shape filling the picture, with the word star printed for toddlers. Ask your child to count the points with one slow finger.

Ask your child

"What shape is this card?" "How many points does the star have?" "Can you twinkle like a star?" "Where do stars live at night?"

What your child can say or do

A five-point count that ends wherever it ends, plus hands twinkling above the head at any mention of the word. Expect star! at every ceiling light for a fortnight.

Out in the real world

The real sky is the free field trip: on a clear evening, look up together and join the card to the sky with a single sentence. Fairy lights and gift wrap keep the indoor supply going.

Try it together

Star factory: fold-none, draw-many — your toddler draws, you cut, and the results get taped to the window. Counting points on their own artwork is the proudest maths there is.

Understanding check

Ask what shape the card is and how many points it has. A star plus any honest point-count passes. A spontaneous twinkle at bedtime is the pass with glitter on it.

Parent tips

Count the points slowly and stop when they run out — the natural ending is the lesson. Never redraw their stars; wobbly lines are the evidence of a first attempt, and first attempts are the treasure.

Staying safe

Star-cutting is grown-up scissors; the toddler runs the drawing and the sticky tape. Window displays go above reaching height, well away from cords and catches.

This lesson pairs with the Star flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shapes (Toddler 3).
